classification.distribution: Tropical and subtropical Asia including India

identification.description: Herb with distinctive dark, flattened reniform seeds; seeds are the principal Ayurvedic drug.
identification.flower: Small bluish-purple flowers in axillary racemes.
identification.fruit: Small pod enclosing a single seed.
identification.seed: Dark brown to black, flattened, reniform seeds.

dosha.pitta: May aggravate; external photosensitization requires caution

therapeutics.precautions: Bakuchi is photosensitizing. External use and phototherapy require qualified supervision; avoid unsupervised exposure to sunlight after topical application.

shlokas:
अवल्गुजो बाकुची स्यात्सोमराजी सुपर्णिका ।
शशिलेखा कृष्णफला सोमा पूतिफलीति च ।
सोमवल्ली कालमेषी कुष्ठघ्नी च प्रकीर्तिता ॥१८०॥
बाकुची मधुरा तिक्ता कटुपाका रसायनी ।
विष्टम्भहृद्धिमा रुच्या सरा श्लेष्मास्रपित्तनुत् ।
रूक्षा हृद्या श्वासकुष्ठमेहज्वरकृमिप्रणुत् ॥१८१॥
तत्फलं पित्तलं कुष्ठकफानिलहरं कटु ।
केश्यं त्वच्यं कृमिश्वासकासशोथामपाण्डुनुत् ॥१८२॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Haritakyadi Varga, verses 180–182 in the searchable recension.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Cullen corylifolium is the currently accepted Kew name; Psoralea corylifolia is a synonym.
modern_information.safety_notes: Photosensitivity is a major safety consideration.
